title: Where to Share Your Presentation Video (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Where to Share Your Presentation Video
slides.notes: You've turned your deck into a video. Now it needs an audience, and where you share it decides who watches to the end.

slides.title: Get the file ready first
bullets: Check the format: MP4, with WebM available
slides.notes: Start with an MP4 and a clear file name, like Q4 onboarding IT setup. Use a strong title slide as the thumbnail, and burn in captions for people watching on mute.

slides.title: Website, YouTube and LinkedIn
bullets: LinkedIn: first few seconds carry the point
slides.notes: Put explainers on your website beside the content they explain. Use YouTube to be found in search, and on LinkedIn, make the first few seconds carry the point.

slides.title: Courses, email and internal tools
bullets: Email: share a link, not an attachment
slides.notes: For courses, place each video beside its activity. By email, send a link and say the length, like a 3-minute walkthrough. Keep confidential videos in approved internal storage.

slides.title: One deck, several versions
bullets: Full version for website, YouTube or LMS
Short version: three to five slides for social
Personalised version with the client's name
slides.notes: You rarely need a brand new video for each channel. Duplicate the deck and adjust it, because the speaker notes do most of the work.

slides.title: Make a version for every channel
slides.notes: Turn one deck into videos for every channel. On Pro, a.i. directs each cut with a tight story and punchy scenes. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
